$description: Snacky App component manifest. Generated from index.html by scripts/generate-agent-files.js - do not hand-edit. Each top-level key is a component id; "v" lists its variants, each with spec values ("s") and real Kotlin/React code samples ("code").

button.name: Button
button.desc: Action triggers for primary, secondary, and tertiary roles, each with an optional Danger intent, in two sizes and four interaction states.
button.usage: Primary is the main CTA. Secondary is for alternative actions (white fill, recolors border/text only). Tertiary is low-emphasis, for toolbars and menus (no fill or border, label color alone). Danger layers onto any hierarchy, e.g. Primary + Danger for a filled destructive CTA; it isn’t a hierarchy of its own. Every combination also has a SLOT for an optional 24×24 icon or social logo, see With Icon / With Social below.

header.name: Header
header.desc: Page header bar with an optional leading back/close icon and an optional trailing action icon.
header.usage: Back drills deeper into a flow and returns to the previous screen; Close dismisses the flow entirely. Right Action only ever pairs with Close, never Back. Title always centers in the remaining space - with a leading icon present, the title row gets matching right padding so the text stays optically centered against the whole bar, not just the leftover space next to the icon.

s.note: Leading icon sits in a 40×40px tappable circle. Back and Close are the same slot with different icon content, not two structurally different variants - see Usage.

badge.name: Badge
badge.desc: Small count and tag indicators: notification pill, discount tag, sold-out overlay, and a static variant label.
badge.usage: Use Notification as an absolute overlay on cart/notification icons to show a numeric count. Use Discount as an inline tag (e.g. on Product Card) to show a percentage-off label. Use Sold Out as an absolute overlay on product images to indicate stock unavailability. Use Variant as a static, non-interactive label showing the currently selected product variant (e.g. "Variant: 75 Grams") - it lives in Figma's Badge frame, not Chips, and has no unselected/clickable state.

accordion.name: Accordion
accordion.desc: Expandable panel for FAQs and collapsible details, with or without a leading icon.
accordion.usage: Collapsed shows a title and a chevron icon; clicking expands content below and rotates the chevron 180°. The expanded panel renders as its own separate elevated card (own radius-field + shadow-md) with a spacing-4 gap below the header, not a padding-only section merged into the header's card. Figma models icon presence as a real variant, not just optional content: With Icon uses a smaller 12px title (smallSemibold) alongside a 24×24px leading logo/icon; No Icon uses the default 14px title (bodySemibold), no leading icon. Neither variant, in either state, ever has a border - elevation alone. In code, both are the same component - the title size responds automatically to whether leadingIcon is passed.

icon.name: Icon
icon.desc: System icon set in two styles - Outline (default/inactive) and Solid (active/selected).
icon.usage: Use Outline as the default state for every icon. Swap to the Solid counterpart of the same name for the active/selected state (Navbar items, filled Favourite, etc). Use 20px for navbar, 24px for buttons and general UI, 16–20px for input fields. Artwork credit: the icon set is UIcons by Flaticon (flaticon.com/uicons), used under CC BY 4.0 and modified (renamed to semantic English names). If you redistribute these icons, that attribution has to come along.

s.use: 42 icons: account, address, back, balance, bell, calendar, camera, cart, cartAdd, category, chat, chevronDown, chevronRight, chevronUp, close, closeInput, creditCard, document, edit, eye, eyeOff, heart, help, history, home, key, lock, logout, map, messageSquare, minus, phone, plus, referral, search, send, sent, share, smartphone, trash, truck, unsent
s.note: Default/inactive state. These are filled outline shapes, not stroked paths: the outline weight is baked into each shape, so they render with a fill and have no stroke width to set. The set is deliberately not uniform, icons are authored at 16, 20 or 24px depending on where they are used (navbar at 20, buttons and general UI at 24, compact input affordances at 16), so each one carries its own viewBox rather than being scaled from a single size.

product-image.name: Product Image
product-image.desc: Context-aware product image component - adapts its frame size and border to where it appears in the UI.
product-image.usage: Pass the usage prop to match the placement. Product-card (128) and product-details (200) render a bare transparent image. List (56) and review (48) wrap the image in a padded frame; review also adds a 1px border. Variant (88) shows the image in a bordered, rounded selection frame. Accordion-modal (24) renders a payment-method logo instead of a product photo. Pass sold to overlay a centered "Sold Out" badge on product-card and product-details.
